4B.
Presentation by Ryan Johnson and Heather Buonomo from the County of San Diego regarding Micro Enterprise Home Kitchens (MEHKO), a program expected to be on the County Board of Supervisor's Agenda in January 2022. A Microenterprise Home Kitchen Operation (MEHKO) is a food facility that is operated by a resident from their private home kitchen. Once permitted, a MEHKO can prepare and serve food to the public from a private residence, similar to a restaurant, as allowed by California State Law (AB626). A MEHKO may serve up to 30 customers per day, or a total of 60 per week.

City Council Member Initiated Item from Deputy Mayor Kranz regarding General Plan Resources Management Element Goal 3, Policy 3.3.
Direct Staff to work with developers to use creative alternatives to the more typical roadway design so that the public right-of-way would be designed with the GPRME goal to not remove or disturb mature trees. This would include using some "Compete Streets" and "traffic calming" tools that are detailed in the Encinitas Neighborhood Traffic Management Program. There also might need to be more done to effectively define what qualifies as a "significant mature tree" so that it becomes an "objective standard" within the scope of the planning approval process.

Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
